## Body

# Managed log ownership precedes rotation

#301 round 1, exact head 8bf2c2d03862cf07ac8aeefd527a3f6c8cdbcbb3:

- A logger initialized before the daemon binds must tolerate two simultaneous initializers. The fact that only one daemon can win the listening port does not serialize earlier destructive file operations.
- Shared `.new`/`.1.new` staging paths plus error cleanup can unlink another initializer's staging/current file. Unique temporary names alone do not establish which process owns the current destination.
- Native private-state replay synchronized two shell launchers before exec, released both into offline daemons on one private port, and reproduced a responsive serving process writing its listening banner to an inode with link count zero. The named log was absent in one run, and held only 260 bytes/no listening banner in the confirming run; unauthenticated health returned 401.
- Verify destination as well as health. A 401 and an alive PID do not prove the daemon's ongoing logs reach the named file.
- Repeat identity must include distinct output destinations. The exact-source Shared/Repeats replay sent the first stderr occurrence entirely into stdout's summary. Global digit folding also conflates distinct panic locations, not just volatile PIDs/counters.
- N2's expanded launch sensor rejects bare constants and parameterized macros, but its closure exemption recognizes any nearby `launch(`/`launch_async(` text, including an unrelated helper. Describe lexical proof limits accurately.

Proof receipts: 13 logger unit tests, both daemon-log e2es, six spawn-site tests, native macOS clippy, private LaunchAgent rotation/restart, ten exact-source scratch controls. Adoption-identity, fresh-mode and inclusive-window mutants compiled and were caught. C25 local quick gate remained dependency/ambient-tool limited; exact-head CI was 5/5.

magicWand: encode the synchronized two-initializer fixture with both health and destination assertions. Keep original-source controls, source-extraction reproductions and full-binary native receipts explicitly separate.

difficulties: a bare shared-build timeout is minutes; use an explicit `s` suffix for seconds. Shared-target lock waits are expected; do independent work, never bypass the lock. Product worktree remained read-only and no production daemon/log was touched.
